chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mu'awiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jarud —
He said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'At what [distance] is the taqsir?' He replied: 'At a barid.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: taqsir: the obligatory shortening of four-rak'a prayers (Dhuhr, 'Asr, 'Isha') to two rak'as during legally qualifying travel
key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: barid: classical Islamic unit of distance equal to 4 farsakhs (~22 km); the minimum distance threshold is debated between one and two barids in Shia fiqh

ai.seo_question: What distance (barid) does Imam al-Baqir specify for the obligation of taqsir (shortening of prayer during travel) in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: Abu al-Jarud asks Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) about the minimum travel distance at which taqsir — the obligatory shortening of four-rak'a prayers to two — becomes applicable. The Imam answers: one barid, a classical unit equal to four farsakhs (approximately 22 km). Al-Shaykh al-Tusi includes this hadith in al-Istibsar (Chapter 133) to address an apparent tension with reports requiring two barids (eight farsakhs); he reconciles them by interpreting this hadith as referring to the single leg of a return journey.
